name: American nationalism
summary: American nationalism treats Americans as a nation that the US government should represent and whose interests it should advance. It combines a civic-creedal core, resting on the Declaration, the Constitution and Lincoln's equality proposition, with cultural-assimilationist and Christian-identity strands, an economic-nationalist tradition of protection and state-built infrastructure, and strong support for the military and for American leadership abroad.
scope: The mainstream family as documented by Wikipedia's survey of strands and the Stanford account of nationalism, drawing on Hamilton and Clay's American System, Lincoln's civic creed and Theodore Roosevelt's New Nationalism, plus contemporary America First nationalism. Strands differ on immigration, religion and economics, so many answers are low confidence or split; it excludes white-nationalist and separatist movements as the mainstream.

keyFigures.name: Alexander Hamilton
keyFigures.role: Architect of the strong national government and the protectionist economic plan later called the American System.

keyFigures.name: Abraham Lincoln
keyFigures.role: Framed civic nationalism through the Declaration and defended the Union.

keyFigures.name: Theodore Roosevelt
keyFigures.role: Promoted the New Nationalism and undivided '100% American' loyalty.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Roosevelt's 1910 programme favoured social-welfare measures, but modern nationalists divide over a state healthcare guarantee, so this is inferred as split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Roosevelt wanted wages above bare subsistence, yet nothing ties the nationalism itself to a statutory minimum; adherents split by party.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Hamilton-Clay lineage used the state to build markets, while modern right nationalists praise markets; the ideology has no single answer.

public-ownership.rationale: Roosevelt wanted corporations regulated, not nationalised, so adherents lean against public ownership; this is inferred, not stated.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Roosevelt backed graduated income and inheritance taxes, but contemporary nationalists mostly oppose raising them; the camps split.

unions-good.rationale: Roosevelt backed workers' welfare but condemned worker violence as firmly as corporate greed; the ideology is not committed on unions.

property-fundamental.rationale: Roosevelt called property the servant of the commonwealth, whereas other adherents treat it as near-sacred; split.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Roosevelt called for publicity, supervised capitalization and control of combinations in the public interest; modern adherents are divided, so the lean is modest.

cut-welfare.rationale: Nationalist movements differ here: welfare for citizens is often defended while dependency is attacked; no settled position.

worker-ownership.rationale: The American System aimed to harmonize agriculture, commerce and industry under existing property forms; worker ownership is not part of it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Post-9/11 nationalism prioritised security and enlistment rose; adherents likely accept counterterrorism surveillance, though this is inferred.

legalize-drugs.rationale: The cultural-nationalist strand favours order and tradition, so adherents lean against legalisation; not a core issue.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Nationalists in the civic-creedal tradition defend free speech as part of the American creed; this is inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Roosevelt described the executive as steward of the public welfare, so adherents favour energetic presidents, though within the Constitution.

state-harmful.rationale: American nationalism holds that the government should represent the nation, so calling the state unnecessary and harmful contradicts it.

limit-guns.rationale: The tradition of armed citizens and the cultural nationalism of current adherents lean against strict gun limits; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Nationalism strongly supports the military, and the lean toward police authority is inferred from its order-and-security emphasis.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Cultural and religious strands lean against; inferred.

decide-locally.rationale: Roosevelt put the national need before sectional advantage and wanted national problems handled nationally; the 1787 nationalists also sought a strong central government.

rehabilitation.rationale: Adherents split between punitive law-and-order and reform views; the ideology is silent.

traditional-family.rationale: Cultural nationalists link national tradition to the family, but this is inferred rather than documented.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Cultural-religious and civic-creedal strands differ and current adherents are split.

abortion-legal.rationale: Adherents split along religious lines; the ideology takes no position.

more-religion-public.rationale: Ardent and restrictive nationalists tie being American to Christianity, but creedal nationalists do not, so the lean is modest.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Creedal nationalists invoke equal citizenship while restrictive nationalists resist remedial programmes; adherents are divided.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Cultural nationalism leans traditional on gender; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Cultural nationalism is a documented core form, and American nationalism pursued assimilation through public schooling and the Pledge.

gradual-change.rationale: Lincoln and Roosevelt both urged reform of institutions while revering them; no clear rule either way.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Restrictive nationalists are the largest surveyed group and US law restricted immigration, but creedal nationalists are far more open, so adherents are split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Nationalism holds that nations deserve self-determination and control over their own affairs, which leans against empowering bodies like the UN.

free-trade.rationale: The economic-nationalist lineage from Hamilton and Clay favoured protection, though some adherents prize free trade.

nation-first.rationale: The ideology is defined as backing the nation's interests and having the government represent the nation, so putting them ahead of global cooperation is central.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Promoting democracy is described as central to American national identity, so adherents often accept intervention, though restrainers dissent.

open-borders.rationale: Nationalism claims a nation's right to control its homeland and favours special duties to co-nationals, which conflicts with eventually open borders.

limit-growth.rationale: The American System aimed at national economic growth; limiting it runs against that tradition.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Current adherents are mostly sceptical of drastic climate programmes, though Roosevelt championed conservation; inferred.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The tradition of internal improvements and industrial progress is optimistic about technology; inferred.

expand-nuclear.rationale: National-strength and infrastructure emphasis suggests support; inferred.

revolution-justified.rationale: The American nation was founded by revolution and Paine's Common Sense helped turn opinion to independence, so adherents accept it in principle.

experts-over-public.rationale: Progressive nationalists trusted expert administration, while populist nationalists distrust experts; split.

central-planning.rationale: The American System was state-supported development within a market, not planning; adherents lean against.

socialized-markets.rationale: Roosevelt sought to control private business rather than transfer ownership; adherents lean against.

land-value-tax.rationale: Nationalist economic programmes relied on tariffs and land sales for revenue, not a land tax.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Roosevelt endorsed a graduated inheritance tax, but modern adherents mostly oppose it; split.

basic-income.rationale: The work-and-citizenship emphasis of nationalism leans against unconditional payments; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protective tariffs were the core of Hamilton's and Clay's programme and are embraced by current America First nationalists.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The American System used federal funds for roads, canals and a national bank to steer national development.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Roosevelt's aim was equal opportunity and fair earnings with broad ownership, but the ideology does not demand it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: The American System built the wage economy, a national bank and protected industry; abolishing money is outside the ideology.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Second Bank of the United States was part of the American System, though some current adherents distrust central banks.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Roosevelt wanted government supervision of corporations but not state-run bodies setting wages and prices; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Lincoln framed the nation as government of, by and for the people, which is incompatible with a single ruling party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The American nation was founded by independence from the Crown and a republican constitution.

democracy-best.rationale: Lincoln's Gettysburg Address makes popular government the nation's purpose, though adherents grumble when voters choose badly.

direct-votes.rationale: The founding nationalists built a representative constitution, so adherents lean toward representation; inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Roosevelt wanted representative bodies to represent all the people, not one class; councils as the basis of power contradict that.

right-to-secede.rationale: The Gettysburg Address presents preserving the Union as the cause worth dying for, so adherents reject a right to secede.

natural-rulers.rationale: Lincoln grounded the nation in the proposition that all men are created equal, which cuts against natural rulers.

political-violence-never.rationale: The nation honours revolution and war, so adherents do not hold political violence is never justified.

war-builds-character.rationale: War surges produced strong nationalism, but modern adherents do not generally endorse war as character-building; split.

separate-church-state.rationale: Adherents split between creedal secularists and those tying Americanness to Christianity.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Christian-identity nationalists exist but the mainstream rests law on the Constitution; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Nationalism has the government representing and defending the nation, so privatised defence conflicts with it.

military-superiority.rationale: The nation's postwar role as a global power and sustained support for its military make superiority a central aim.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Creedal nationalism, the nation-of-immigrants tradition, opposes it, though ethnocultural strands have historically favoured a European-descended nation.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Clay's aim was to harmonize agriculture, commerce and industry, and nationalism treats the nation as one body, not warring classes.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Roosevelt stressed equal opportunity and income fairly earned, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Nationalism asserts the nation's authority over its territory; inferred.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Nationalists generally resist reparations as a foreign claim on national resources; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Nationalism centres on the nation-state's self-determination, not union with other nations; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Nationalism praises national interest; individual self-interest as virtue is not part of it.

duties-before-rights.rationale: The creedal tradition rests on rights, though duty to nation is stressed; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Roosevelt's conservation was stewardship for the nation, not intrinsic value; adherents split.

limit-population.rationale: Nationalist emphasis on national strength leans against population limits; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The tradition embraced industry and internal improvement.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Adherents are mixed on disruptive speed; the ideology is silent.

human-enhancement.rationale: No stated position; cultural traditionalists oppose, others are open.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The nation is described as government by the people, so algorithmic rule is disfavoured; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Security hawks and civil libertarians split within the tradition.

restore-past-order.rationale: Lincoln looked to the founders but sought a new birth of freedom; current adherents mix restoration and progress.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Clay and Hamilton were pragmatic state-builders, but the ideology has no stance on judging policy.

direct-action.rationale: The nation's political creed works through elections and constitutional institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: Neither the founding documents nor the Roosevelt tradition address whether methods must mirror aims, so adherents have no settled view.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Industrial development was central to the American System.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The American System built specialized national industry and trade.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Roosevelt held that no one should receive income not fairly earned, and the tradition rewards work.

production-for-use.rationale: Protected private industry and a national bank presume production for the market.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Roosevelt condemned speculative gain yet defended earned profit and combinations under control, rejecting a general exploitation thesis.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Government of the people for the people is incompatible with class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Clay's American System expected independent Western farmers selling to factory workers.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The American System treats commerce and industry as national assets, not causes of war.

taxation-theft.rationale: The American System funded national projects through tariffs and land sales, accepting taxation as legitimate.

harm-principle.rationale: Adherents split between libertarian and cultural-conservative views on policing morals.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The creed stresses individual rights, but nationalism also asserts the nation's claims; split.

conscription.rationale: World War I conscription met little resistance and nationalism treats service as duty; inferred for peacetime.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nationalists value voice and loyalty to the nation; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: Roosevelt's steward-of-welfare state and the Hamiltonian state are not business-like, but some modern adherents like the idea; split.

positive-liberty.rationale: Roosevelt's human-welfare language leans positive, while modern adherents lean negative; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Contemporary right nationalists say yes while civic nationalists do not; split.

hereditarian-race.rationale: The creedal mainstream rejects racial hierarchies, though ethnocultural strands have held them; inferred.

organic-representation.rationale: The tradition is territorial parties and elections, not corporate representation.

total-state.rationale: The nation is conceived as government of the people with limits, not an all-directing state.

national-rebirth.rationale: Lincoln called for a new birth of freedom and current slogans speak of national renewal, but adherents differ on decadence framing.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Manifest Destiny was historic nationalism but modern adherents split between restraint and influence abroad.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The nation rests on the consent of equal citizens, not personal fealty.

bound-labor.rationale: Lincoln's creed of equality and freedom rejects forced bound labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Nationalist cultural traditionalists mostly reject it; inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: The creed appeals to universal truths such as equality, though not framed as cross-cultural philosophy.

single-common-good.rationale: Roosevelt invoked a national good above sectional interest, but pluralist politics is accepted too.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: The ideology has no position; adherents' views follow other commitments.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Not addressed; nationalism asserts a nation's right to control entry.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not a matter for an English-speaking nation, so no stated position.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Roosevelt sought regulation and fair wages, not worker votes on management.

school-vouchers.rationale: Adherents are split over school choice.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Hamilton accepted national debt and the American System spent on improvements, while modern adherents differ.

economic-freedom.rationale: Roosevelt subordinated property to welfare while other adherents insist on economic freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: The constitutional republic relies on law and representatives.

national-self-determination.rationale: The Stanford entry lists self-determination as a core nationalist claim, and American nationalism rests on independence.

force-without-un.rationale: Nation-first sovereignty favours freedom of action abroad, though adherents split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Adherents split between secular creed and religious identity.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Nationalists hold special duties owed to co-nationals, which favours reserving benefits for citizens.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Roosevelt condemned unearned income, which suggests work requirements; inferred.

class-collaboration.rationale: Clay sought to harmonize interests and Roosevelt held both capital and labor to account.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Cultural nationalism prizes inherited national institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: American nationalism sees the US as leading power, not dominated.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism organises loyalty along national lines rather than class lines.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Equal citizenship is the creed's mainstream despite traditional strands.

ban-interest.rationale: The American System relied on a national bank and credit.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The creed of equal citizenship rejects it, despite historic ethnocultural exclusions.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The nation's state is held to represent all the people.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: America First nationalism backs domestic energy output; inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Roosevelt demanded "100% American" loyalty and public schools and the Pledge pursued assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim held at the fringe; the mainstream does not endorse it.

proportional-representation.rationale: The tradition of single-member districts is unquestioned; inferred.

national-mission.rationale: Promoting democracy is described as central to American identity and exceptionalism.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not part of the nationalist account.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Contemporary populist nationalists say yes, while civic nationalists defend the political class; the ideology itself is split.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics once drew some US support but is not part of the creed today.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Nationalists tend to defend the nation's military and police.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The American System has a state building a bank and infrastructure.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Equal citizenship under the creed contradicts it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The Gettysburg Address dedicates the nation to the proposition that all men are created equal.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; nationalists reject socialism generally.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation's founding as legitimate.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: One law for all citizens suits a shared national citizenship.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Religious liberty is part of the American creed; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not an American concern; the culture opposes it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Adherents split on religion in public schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist state is outside the scope of the ideology.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Lincoln's government of, by and for the people rests on popular consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Protection aimed at building domestic industry and a favourable balance, as in Trump-era thinking; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Conflicts with equal citizenship and the creed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The nation accepts war and military force.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Nationalists mix Darwinist and cooperative views.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The tradition favours free political competition.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: The republican tradition fits but is not stated.

separated-powers.rationale: The nationalists of 1787 built the Constitution with separate branches and checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Popular government by and for the people contradicts vanguard rule.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Roosevelt prioritised human welfare, though adherents differ.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Promotion of broad home ownership fits equal opportunity; inferred.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Roosevelt condemned worker violence but supported workers' welfare.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Roosevelt blamed institutions and privilege, not numbers.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Restrictive and ardent nationalists say yes, creedal nationalists say no.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Lincoln faced the question in the Civil War, and adherents are divided.

party-controls-media.rationale: Government by the people presumes free expression.

party-commands-army.rationale: The military serves the nation and its constitution, not a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalization was historically easy yet restrictionists want more; split.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: American parties are loose and the tradition values independent representatives.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Self-determination is a core nationalist claim, so pooling sovereignty in a union contradicts it.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The president commands the forces and Roosevelt called the executive steward of public welfare.

church-by-bishops.rationale: No stated position; irrelevant to the ideology.

clerical-rule.rationale: Government of the people excludes clerical authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: In both world wars pacifists and dissenters largely set aside objections and supported the nation.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The tradition protects free expression, though cultural nationalists push back.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: The republic keeps limits on tenure; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Progressive era fans favoured it, others not.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Postwar nationalism accepted alliances while America First nationalists question them; split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Clay's coalition combined farmers and manufacturers.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Lincoln's Union cause is closely analogous, yet no stance on others.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Populist strands say yes, others not.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Cultural nationalism prizes the national culture over others.

death-penalty.rationale: Law-and-order stance of many adherents; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: American nationalism takes no stance on science curricula; religious-identity adherents say yes and civic ones say no.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Split between cultural conservatives and civil-liberties views.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The US tradition of birth-based citizenship cuts against it, though restrictive nationalists define Americans as US-born.

religious-exemptions.rationale: The nationalist tradition stresses shared law for all, but religious liberty also matters to adherents, so they split.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The ideology stresses shared national culture but also liberty, and does not address social pressure to conform; split.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Nation-first nationalism leans against forgiving foreign debts owed to the US, though the ideology never addressed the question.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The nation values its existing constitution, but no position.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Liberty is part of the creed.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Special duties to co-nationals weigh against general aid duties.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: The US is a leading military power and nationalism supports military superiority.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Hamilton founded a national bank, yet modern adherents differ.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The ideology says nothing on foreign territorial disputes, so any stance is inferred and adherents are split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Roosevelt called property servant of the commonwealth, although the lean varies.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A debate among Marxists that American nationalism has no stake in; it simply opposes the Soviet system.

collective-defense.rationale: Postwar US nationalism supported alliances such as NATO; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The ideology has no position on annexation disputes elsewhere, and its own history of expansion makes adherents divided.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Religious liberty is part of the creed.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The US president is both head of state and partisan; no settled view.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The Gettysburg Address frames the war as preserving the Union.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Roosevelt backed graduated income taxes while many modern adherents prefer flat rates; the ideology is split.

character-from-environment.rationale: American nationalism has no doctrine on nature versus nurture, though its assimilation policies imply upbringing matters.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The nation is a constitutional republic of equal citizens.

space-expansion.rationale: National-power rhetoric favours space leadership, but the ideology lacks any stated position on it.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The 1787 Constitution blended elements, though not stated this way.

leader-cult.rationale: A republican civic tradition distrusts leader worship.

equal-parenting.rationale: A family-law question the ideology never addressed, with adherents divided between traditionalist and equality views.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A question internal to Marxism that American nationalism never addresses; it rejects socialism broadly.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not part of the programme; inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: The ideology does not address foreign refugee questions, and its stance on controlling entry makes any answer an inference.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Religious liberty belongs to the American creed.

women-must-cover.rationale: Individual liberty is part of the creed.

common-currency.rationale: Retained national sovereignty is part of the nationalist claim.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Nationalists want a nation-state, not union by ancestry.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: American nationalism has no stated view on whether persecuted minorities should emigrate, so adherents are split.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The tradition credits ideas such as the founding proposition.

ban-cartels.rationale: Roosevelt held combinations an economic necessity to control, not break up.

no-bailouts.rationale: Hamiltonian state support for credit contrasts with populist anger at bailouts, so adherents are divided.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The constitutional tradition accepts limits on majorities.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Split between protectionists and trade-standards advocates.

moral-incentives.rationale: Market incentives and protection are used.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Popular consent is the ground of legitimacy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Lincoln grounded the nation in equality of all men.

history-own-civilization.rationale: American nationalism treats Americans as the nation to be served, so schools telling the national story, with Lincoln and the founding at its centre, are favoured.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Roosevelt-era nationalists defended temporary rule in the Philippines, but the creedal and America First strands reject it; adherents split.

patriotic-education.rationale: Public schooling and the Pledge were used to build loyalty and pride in nation and flag, and this is a defining nationalist aim.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Lincoln's equality proposition and the colorblind creedal strand favour judging individuals equally, but the strands differ; inferred.

public-money-creation.rationale: Hamilton and Clay backed a national bank, but money creation by a public body is not an established nationalist position; adherents split.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism sought regulation and reform to save capitalism from its excesses, implying it can adapt; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The republic arose against empire and nationalists emphasise American, not Anglo, leadership, so influence in Britain's former lands is not a nationalist aim; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: The American System sought protection and self-reliance for the US; for poor countries inferred as favouring national self-sufficiency over dependence, though not stated.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Roosevelt held that workers are part of the nation sharing its interest and were due fair treatment, not a class set against it; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Lincoln's equality proposition and civic nationalism imply equal treatment in public life, though economic nationalists respect property; inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Creedal nationalists treat the Constitution and Declaration as the nation's founding charter whose rights bind government.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred: nationalists favour settled borders and treaties and dislike reopening the past.

elective-rulers.rationale: Lincoln's government of the people, by the people, for the people places rule on popular election.

minority-veto.rationale: The Gettysburg Address defends preserving the Union against secession, which rejects a dissenting-part veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from the Declaration-based national creed; Gettysburg invokes a new birth of freedom, but resistance was not tested here.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The statement presumes a monarch; American nationalists value Congress but also separation of powers and executive stewardship under Roosevelt.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred; not defining for American nationalism.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred; mainstream strands accept humane animal agriculture and research.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism put human welfare above property and called on the wealthy to serve the common good.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Gettysburg calls on the living to dedicate themselves to the unfinished work, a civic duty to take part.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred: a critical-theory claim that mainstream nationalists reject.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred: a Gramscian claim that nationalists reject.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The American System sought development through protection and national investment, not dependency; inferred rejection of the thesis.

native-born-offices.rationale: Only the presidency requires natural birth; nativist and civic strands differ on wider offices.

party-own-road.rationale: The ideology never addressed this issue, so it is inferred as neutral from its principles.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The American System aimed at national self-sufficiency through protection and internal improvements.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred: mainstream nationalists do not usually make irredentist demands.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Civic nationalism grounds membership in shared principles, not descent, and no nationalist strand gives political leadership by ancestry.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Anti-communist and anti-fascist tradition leads many nationalists to condemn both; contested.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Lincoln framed the war as for the equality proposition and the end of slavery, though revisionist strands differ.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Contemporary nationalists are split between preserving monuments and civic reappraisal.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not a defining issue; strands split.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not a defining issue; strands split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Creedal nationalists hold universal principles, while realist and ardent strands stress distinct institutions; split.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Inferred from American civilian control of the military.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from traditional strands; not addressed by the ideology.

filial-duty.rationale: Family values are part of the conservative strand of American nationalism, though no source states a filial duty; inferred from that.

office-by-exam.rationale: American civic tradition fills most offices by election and nationalists do not generally favour examination-selected rule; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The American System tradition of protecting national industry and today's America First economic nationalism favour shielding strategic firms; inferred from that.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Nationalism does not address divorce law and adherents split between social conservatives and others; inferred as split.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The creedal republic is one of representatives under constitutional limits, not instructed delegates recallable at will; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: America First nationalists have mostly defended the state pension rather than privatising it, though some conservatives differ; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism subordinates property to human welfare but keeps private ownership, and the American System rested on individual land holding.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Government by and for the people under the constitutional creed includes legislative control of the purse; inferred from the creed.

single-official-language.rationale: Ardent nationalists hold that a true American must speak English and assimilation is a core theme, but creedal nationalists set fewer restrictions.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Reserving land for citizens fits the nation-first stance of the ardent strands, but the point is not stated in the sources; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Mainstream nationalists, who rest national unity on equality of rights, tend to see discrimination as unequal treatment; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The nationalist family has no settled view on consumer culture; some strands criticise it and economic nationalists celebrate growth.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Cold War American nationalism saw the country as a world police against communism, including the Bay of Pigs operation, so backing hostile-state insurgents is within the tradition.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Nationalism stresses national self-determination, so forcibly keeping allies in line cuts against it, though hemispheric interventions are an exception; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Theodore Roosevelt's New Nationalism called for ending corporate control of politics and special-interest influence over government.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Nationalists generally favour guarding sovereignty from foreign influence; inferred from the nationalist core.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: America First and civic strands favour pro-family policy over immigration to offset decline; strands differ, so inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: The property and free-movement tradition of the Republic opposes residency-based bars, though economic nationalists might accept some; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Roosevelt favoured social protections but a federal job guarantee is not a stated nationalist position; strands split.

democratic-peace.rationale: Lincolnian nationalists hold America as the last best hope of free government, while America First strands are sceptical of democracy promotion; split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The civic creed rests on the Constitution and rule of law, so a typical adherent would affirm a general duty to obey; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Strong support for American leadership and the military abroad means rejecting a blanket ban on intervention, though America First strands restrain it.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Mainstream American nationalism is civic-creedal and excludes white-nationalist conspiracy theories as the mainstream; inferred.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The Christian-identity and cultural strands favour traditional marriage, so abolishing legal marriage would be rejected; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The Gettysburg ideal of government of the people suggests accountable, open government; inferred.

local-production.rationale: The American System of protection and internal improvements aimed to build a home market and domestic industry.

informal-organisation.rationale: Nationalism stresses a unified national organisation and institutions, not loose informal groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Nationalists in the America First strand give the Constitution and national sovereignty precedence over international bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: The civic-creedal core defines the nation by the Declaration and Constitution, though a Christian-identity strand disagrees.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Nationalism stresses US sovereignty and equal standing; the tribute system is the opposite of how the sources treat the nation's place in the world.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The American System tied regions into national finance and internal improvements, but modern strands differ; inferred as split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism and the American System defend private property; common ownership of production is inferred as rejected.

defeat-communism.rationale: Strong military and American leadership abroad characterise the nationalism; opposition to communism is inferred from them.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Roosevelt and later strands accept private actors in public ends; inferred.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Christian-identity strand holds religion central to American identity; inferred as disagreeing.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The American System and the New Nationalism both treat industrial capitalism as the base of national greatness, with regulation.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The creedal strand reads equality as civil and political; economic transformation is inferred as rejected.

socialized-care.rationale: Roosevelt favoured welfare measures but not public housework; inferred as rejected.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Assimilationist strands stress English but American nationalism has no purge programme; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Strands diverge between treaty fidelity and national sovereignty over internal nations; inferred as split.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Nationalism centres on the nation-state and market or private property; inferred.

majority-settlement.rationale: No source ties mainstream American nationalism to steering majority settlement in minority regions; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism regulated capitalism rather than rejecting it, and communism is rejected; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Civic-creedal nationalists ground the nation in the Declaration's principles rather than ancestral land, while other strands invoke Christian or cultural heritage; inferred as split.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No strand of American nationalism endorses Holocaust denial; the movement's civic core and wartime patriotism stand opposed to it, inferred from the sources' account of strands.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not a nationalist issue; the civic creed stresses equal rights and modern adherents mostly oppose criminalising private conduct, inferred.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The civic creed rests on government of, by and for the people and constitutional liberties, which Lincoln's Gettysburg Address affirms, so suppressing opposition contradicts it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The Constitution's religious-liberty guarantees are part of the civic creed that mainstream American nationalism venerates, so punishing blasphemy conflicts with it.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The American System aimed at national development at home, but Roosevelt-era expansion treated territories as national assets; typical adherents today reject exploitative rule, inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Never addressed; a religious duty specific to Islam is not part of American nationalism, and adherents would not take it as a shared principle, inferred.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Not addressed; a civic nation governed by a secular constitution does not accept removal of rulers for lacking religious law, inferred from the creed.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism backed direct democracy devices like primaries, but the creed is representative government and nationalists split on direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Nationalists emphasise common national identity over group-based analyses of overlapping oppressions, inferred from the unitary-nation framing.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not a defining issue; contemporary nationalists lean against recognition by gender identity, though civic strands vary.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents split by party and religion, so inferred as split.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism sought to combine the best of competing camps, but nationalists generally align with the right, so adherents split.

alienated-labor.rationale: The movement does not frame capitalism as alienating; it favours national capitalism and protection, inferred from the American System.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Christian-identity strands see Islam as incompatible while the civic strand welcomes anyone who accepts the creed; adherents are split.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The Declaration cites a Creator, but Lincoln's formula is government of the people, so authority is held to come from the people; Christian-identity strands dissent.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Nationalists tend to oppose restrictions on religious expression by officials and students, inferred from the emphasis on Christian identity and free exercise.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not addressed; Roosevelt favoured worker protections but modern nationalists split by party on employer regulation.

social-market-economy.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism paired regulation of corporations with social welfare and the American System paired markets with state action, inferred as a middle path.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The summary records strong support for the military; abolishing armed forces is incompatible with a nationalism built on national strength.

rich-first.rationale: The American System aimed at balanced national growth, but nationalists are split on tolerating regional or personal inequality, inferred.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: America First strands favour staying out of blocs while others support alliances and American leadership, so adherents are split.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The civic creed of the Declaration and Gettysburg's 'government of the people' makes hereditary succession to office alien to American nationalism.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from the American System's national bank and Roosevelt's state-regulatory outlook, which favoured public or national credit institutions over user-owned mutual banks; the topic is not addressed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from America First nationalism's stress on national economic sovereignty; strands differ and the sources do not address lender conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: Lincoln's equality proposition and the civic creed point to broad citizen voting, and wealth tests are not part of the nationalist tradition.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Not addressed by American nationalism; inferred that its typical adherents do not accept a theory linking women's and nature's domination.

reification.rationale: Inferred from Roosevelt's acceptance of regulated property and markets; the sources do not discuss reification, a Marxist concept.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Roosevelt attacked the power of corporate wealth over politics but nationalists today divide on media ownership; inferred as split.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Government under the Constitution and fixed law is central to the civic-creedal core, though some strands accept executive discretion.

racial-franchise.rationale: The mainstream civic-creedal nationalism, resting on the equality proposition, rejects race-limited voting; white-nationalist strands are outside this audit's scope.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents are split on online participation, inferred from the general nationalist emphasis on existing constitutional institutions.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the Gettysburg ideal of government of the people; the sources do not address open data directly.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not part of the American nationalist tradition, whose civic creed protects religious liberty; inferred from the Constitution-centred core.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: targeting businesses by owners' religion contradicts the civic creed and equality proposition; the sources do not address it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Mainstream American nationalism rests on the constitutional republic of elected representatives and the Founders' wariness of pure democracy; lotteried assemblies are not discussed in the sources, so this is inferred from that tradition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Christian-identity and cultural strands favour preserving inherited religious tradition, though the civic-creedal strand is indifferent; inferred from the sources' emphasis on a shared Christian heritage.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism attacked the power of great fortunes over government and called for regulation, and Lincoln's tradition favours broad opportunity.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Contemporary strands split: civic nationalists accept service by any citizen while Christian-identity and cultural strands object.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: American nationalism's mainstream, including its Christian-identity strand, treats religion as part of national life, and no strand backs state atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The nationalist emphasis on order, law and a strong state leaves no strand favouring abolition of police and prisons.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the single-nation, majority-rule civic model, which resists group-based power-sharing between communities.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Split: the Hamilton and Roosevelt tradition favours active federal programmes while contemporary conservative strands favour private and local help.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from the republican, anti-elite strand of the American tradition and the popularity of term limits in contemporary America First politics; strands do not treat it as defining.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from the attachment to the constitutional representative republic, with no source showing support for liquid democracy.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not a theme of the tradition; some adherents back it as national security, others see it as a distraction from national interests.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Religious-institution governance is not a nationalist question and adherents belong to denominations that differ on the matter.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the civic-creedal equality tradition and modern American norms, though Christian-identity strands hold more traditional views.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: American nationalism treats membership as citizenship and its national interest as that of citizens, so voting for non-citizens is inferred as opposed.

rent-control.rationale: The American System and mainstream strands favour state-built infrastructure and protection but not price controls; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: The Constitution's patent and copyright clause is a national tradition and Hamilton's programme favoured protecting domestic invention, so abolition is inferred as strongly rejected.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism valued national efficiency and service, but drilled uniformed state youth movements are not a mainstream American demand.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Mainstream American nationalists back the US nuclear deterrent and strong military, so a ban on basing nuclear weapons at home is inferred as disliked.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Sovereignty-focused America First strands object to foreign forces on American soil, though the US itself maintains bases abroad; inferred.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Strands split on recognising historical atrocities abroad and whether recognition serves the national interest.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Lincoln held labour prior to capital and Roosevelt's New Nationalism put human welfare above property rights, so income for work is inferred as agreeable.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Strong support for the military and national defence, and a tradition of armed defence, imply strong rejection of the absolute claim.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The creedal core presents America as a new nation founded in 1776 on an idea, not an ancient continuous one; cultural strands differ.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Mainstream American nationalists tend to hold that sex is biological; the issue is not a feature of the doctrine and is inferred.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The statement is outside the doctrine; strands differ.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Fallen soldiers are honoured as the nation's dead at Gettysburg and in civic religion, though sainthood language fits only some strands.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The Christian strand sees politics as moral struggle while the civic strand does not, so the strands split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: American nationalism treats the US as a settled nation-state that gathers its people, not as a cultural centre for a diaspora; inferred.

culture-before-state.rationale: Hamilton and Clay built the state and Lincoln defended the Union, so the state came first in the tradition.

god-not-male.rationale: The Christian-identity strand favours traditional language and the civic strand is indifferent, so the strands split.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The issue is outside the doctrine and strands differ.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The civic-creedal core rejects reserving economic life to an ethnic or national majority, though some strands lean the other way.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: American nationalism rests on a single territorial federation of states, not on regions merged by people; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: American nationalist strands divide; Roosevelt's New Nationalism backed labour but modern nationalists are split on unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Inferred from mainstream American nationalism's rejection of socialism and its stress on the nation's shared civic creed.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Roosevelt favoured public regulation of utilities, but present-day strands are split on public provision.

second-chamber.rationale: The US Constitution that the civic creed reveres has a Senate alongside the House, and nationalists treat it as a sound design.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the American System's support for private enterprise and national development rather than communal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from Hamilton and Clay's nationalist preference for a strong national government over loose confederation.

family-wage.rationale: Roosevelt's 1910 speech backed a living wage, but modern nationalist strands differ on the wage a worker should earn.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic and not a defining issue; America First nationalists are split on regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not a defining issue and not addressed by sources; inferred as split.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not a nationalist issue; contemporary strands are split between privacy and security concerns.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not a nationalist issue; strands are split.

person-over-state.rationale: The creedal core rests on the Declaration's equal rights of the individual, though nationalism also asks sacrifice for the nation.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Christian-identity and civic-religion strands affirm it, though the civic core is not explicitly spiritual.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Nationalists favour a strong union, but the American tradition also protects state powers, so adherents are split.

gm-crops.rationale: Not a nationalist issue; strands are split.

dense-cities.rationale: Not a nationalist issue; strands are split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The mainstream civic-creedal core rejects racial grouping, and white-nationalist strands are excluded from the scope.

racial-pride.rationale: Mainstream strands stress national rather than racial pride, and conservatives are split on pride in ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: American nationalism supports a strong military and leadership abroad, and Roosevelt stood for assertive use of force, though some America First strands favour restraint.

language-defines-nation.rationale: American nationalism is civic-creedal at its core and treats the US as one nation of many origins, so shared language alone does not define a nation; inferred from the Wikipedia survey and Lincoln's proposition.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the civic creed of one American people under one Constitution, which runs against separate religious electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Mainstream strands do not hold that foreign powers aim to break up the US; some America First voices stress foreign threats, so adherents are split. Inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: Nothing in the nationalist sources addresses tuition; adherents split by party, with the American System tradition favouring public education but modern nationalists divided. Inferred.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: the Rooseveltian tradition favoured conservation through regulation and public management, and modern nationalists are wary of new taxes.

future-generations.rationale: Theodore Roosevelt's New Nationalism stressed conserving national resources for future citizens; inferred as a mild agreement.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources do not address this and adherents are split between traditional and egalitarian views. Inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: Strong support for the military and American strength abroad makes minimum-level disarmament unlikely; inferred from the survey of strands.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Nationalists generally value executive freedom in foreign affairs over a ban on secret agreements; inferred from the emphasis on national interest.

capital-controls.rationale: The American System tradition backed state-directed national economic strength, but modern nationalists split on controlling capital flows. Inferred.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the civic creed of one constitutional government under law; mainstream strands accept state forces but gun-rights strands resist broad disarmament.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist view that citizens owe service to the nation, as in Lincoln's call to finish the work for which soldiers died.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Strands differ: Roosevelt's New Nationalism backed labour protection while other strands favour individual contracts.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Contemporary strands split; Roosevelt favoured protecting working families and America First strands do not agree on it.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Strands differ; Hamilton and Roosevelt favoured active national finance while contemporary strands vary.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred from nation-first and America First positions, which oppose reshaping international economic rules for others.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The American creed holds the Constitution as the nation's foundation, so smashing the state is rejected.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Strands differ; the American System favoured national direction while others favour free experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not a stated position of the family; strands split.

sacred-nation.rationale: Lincoln's address speaks of a nation conceived in liberty and a 'new birth of freedom' for which the dead gave their last full measure, treating the nation as an enduring, quasi-sacred community.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from the family's opposition to broad redistribution programmes; Roosevelt's nationalism favoured other means.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred from its view of the nation as one community with shared interests, so regional exploitation is not framed in colonial terms.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the founding creed that all men are created equal and so hold shared rights.

public-service-media.rationale: Strands split; the nationalist family has no settled position on public broadcasting.

religions-one-truth.rationale: American nationalism is civic and treats religion as a matter of belief, not a claim about shared truth; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: The American System and Roosevelt's New Nationalism favoured active national economic support for producers, though strands differ; inferred.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Contemporary America First nationalism prizes national strength and sovereignty, so it keeps the arsenal; inferred.

workers-own-party.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism sought one national interest above class, so a separate workers' party cuts against it; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Gettysburg's proposition that all are created equal supports legal protection of girls and women; inferred.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The equality proposition implies equal property rights for women; inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: American nationalism has no position on how regional languages are named; inferred.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Roosevelt's New Nationalism called for federal regulation of corporations rather than leaving it to private suits; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Gettysburg's government of, by and for the people leaves lawmaking to representatives of the people; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Civic nationalism values individual liberty, though conservationist strands differ; inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Contemporary nationalist strands favour tough law-and-order measures; inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Nationalist strands expect immigrants to assimilate and learn English, though civic strands prefer encouragement; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Strands differ: economic nationalists and the populist right are split on right-to-work, and nothing ties the nationalism itself to either side.

voter-id.rationale: Contemporary America First nationalism backs citizenship-based voting rules, though the older civic creed strand is less concerned; inferred.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The civic-creedal core rests on equality and the Constitution's religious neutrality, though the Christian-identity strand dissents, so this is contested.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Lincoln's government of the people implies rule by electoral consent, but strands differ on whether policies such as national interest also matter.

premarital-sex.rationale: Adherents split between the cultural-traditionalist strand and the civic strand; the nationalism is not defined by a view on this.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the national-security emphasis of the military and foreign-policy strand, though civic-libertarian adherents would dissent.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The American System used the state to build the economy, but modern adherents split on welfare reform, so this is inferred as split.

women-suffrage.rationale: Lincoln's equality proposition and the civic creed underpin equal citizenship, and the mainstream movement accepts women's full political rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Inferred; the Christian-identity strand would reject this and the civic strand is indifferent.

race-social-construct.rationale: Strands differ sharply: the civic strand is open to this while ethnocultural strands are not, so it is split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Roosevelt's programme backed new federal regulatory bodies, but modern nationalists split on gender-specific agencies, so this is inferred as split.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should give their undivided loyalty to the nation rather than to a hyphenated or foreign identity.
missingStatements.rationale: Roosevelt demanded Americans be '100% American' rather than hyphenated, and public schooling and the Pledge pursued this loyalty.

missingStatements.text: National membership should rest on shared political principles rather than ancestry or religion.
missingStatements.rationale: Lincoln tied national unity to the Declaration's equality proposition and creedal nationalists place the fewest restrictions on who counts, though ardent strands disagree.

notes: Creedal, ardent and restrictive strands answer differently on immigration, religion, diversity and race; the profile follows the mainstream and marks contested items low.
